answer: In a 403(b) or 457(b), you can contribute pre-tax money from your paycheck to your plan account and invest it. The contributions and their investment earnings are not taxed until you withdraw the money, typically after retirement. This is called tax-deferred growth: taxes are postponed, not eliminated.
